mainEntity.name: How much does a Land Rover Defender 90 TD5 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt Land Rover Defender 90 TD5 engine typically costs between £3,500 and £5,500 for supply only. Reconditioned units start around £2,500, while used engines can be found from £800. Prices vary based on the specific engine code and whether you choose supply-only or a full supply and fit service.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of head gasket failure in a Land Rover Defender 90 TD5?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early warning signs include white smoke from the exhaust, unexplained coolant loss, and oil that appears milky or frothy. In severe cases, the shearing of the plastic head dowels causes the cylinder head to lift, leading to a sudden loss of compression and engine misfires.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Land Rover Defender 90 TD5?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, given the current classic vehicle market. A well-maintained Land Rover Defender 90 TD5 holds a value of £8,000 to £18,000+. Investing £3,500-£5,500 in a rebuilt engine with a 12-month warranty is financially viable and protects the appreciating asset value of the vehicle, unlike a cheap used engine with no guarantee.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the 10P and 15P Land Rover Defender 90 TD5 engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are 2.5-litre, 122hp inline-five diesel engines. The primary difference is that the later 15P (introduced in 2002) features upgraded steel head locating dowels to prevent the head gasket failures common in the earlier 10P. However, both codes remain susceptible to the injector loom oil leak issue.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Land Rover Defender 90 TD5 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for a Land Rover Defender 90 TD5 typically takes 2 to 3 working days. This includes the removal of the old unit, thorough cleaning of the engine bay, installation of the replacement engine, and comprehensive testing to ensure all systems are functioning correctly.

historyTimeline.h2: Land Rover Defender 90 TD5 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: Launched in 1998, the Land Rover Defender 90 TD5 brought electronic fuel injection and refined low-end torque to the iconic short-wheelbase 4x4, replacing the naturally aspirated 300Tdi. Its 2.5-litre inline-five diesel remained the sole powerplant for this variant until the Puma generation update in 2007.

milestones.description: 10P engine code introduced, 2.5L, 122hp (replaced 300Tdi with electronic management and improved refinement)
15P engine code introduced, 2.5L, 122hp (updated with steel head locating dowels and a revised injector harness to address early reliability concerns)
Final model year for the classic Land Rover Defender 90 TD5 before the 2007 Puma (2.4 TDCi) generation took over

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Land Rover Defender 90 TD5 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Land Rover Defender 90 TD5 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Land Rover Defender 90 TD5 is a robust workhorse, but its 2.5-litre inline-five diesel has two well-documented Achilles heels: head gasket failure and ECU oil contamination. Rebuilt engines sourced through EnginesMarket include upgraded components, such as steel locating dowels and revised wiring harnesses, specifically addressing these original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Head Gasket Failure - Why the Land Rover Defender 90 TD5 10P Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The original plastic head locating dowels shear under thermal stress, allowing the cylinder head to lift and the gasket to fail, often resulting in coolant loss and white smoke.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Head bolt torque check and upgraded steel dowel installation (if caught early)
repairOptions.longevity: Temporary fix; only suitable if no block or head warping has occurred

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded steel dowels, new head gasket, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The definitive solution for catastrophic failure or warped components

problems.recommendation: If your ECU is intact, replacing the injector loom is a highly cost-effective preventative measure. However, if the head gasket has failed and the engine has overheated, a full rebuilt unit with upgraded steel dowels is the only reliable long-term solution to prevent recurrence.

problems.h4: Injector Loom Oil Leak - Why the Land Rover Defender 90 TD5 ECU Fails
problems.affectedModels: Land Rover Defender 90 TD5 (10P and early 15P, 1998-2004)
problems.rootCause: The injector wiring harness insulation degrades, allowing engine oil to wick up the copper strands directly into the Engine Control Unit (ECU), causing electrical shorts and no-start conditions.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of the injector loom and ECU pin cleaning
repairOptions.longevity: Highly effective if the ECU is not permanently damaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit with revised wiring harness pre-installed, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if the ECU is destroyed or the engine has suffered secondary damage
